signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Yield Spread
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags USD outperforming peers with a 1W average of +0.643% across 9 pairs while SEK lags at −0.648% across 2 pairs, establishing a 1.290% bilateral spread. USD/SEK trades at 9.773, holding firmly above its rising SMA20 at 9.576 and SMA50 at 9.592. The Fed policy rate of 3.75% against the Riksbank at 1.75% delivers a +200bp nominal carry advantage to the dollar, reinforced by a real policy rate differential of +1.67% (US +1.35% vs SEK −0.32%). Sweden's Economic Surprise Index sits at −29.2, reflecting persistent macroeconomic data misses that contrast with steady US economic performance. The bilateral gap represents the dominant performance dispersion across G10 currencies this week. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; carry advantage and macro divergences underpin bilateral trend. Catalyst: FOMC interest rate decision 16 Sep — hold widely expected. Risk: Fed signals accelerated easing cycle, compressing the 200bp policy differential.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Bear Steepener
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.27, situated below its SMA20 at 157.14, SMA50 at 159.40, and SMA200 at 158.39. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal prints at −1.98, displaying an acute put skew as the options market pays up for base downside protection despite a +264bp OIS carry premium favoring the dollar (SOFR 3.62% vs TONA 0.98%). Leveraged funds expanded net short JPY positioning by +58,042 contracts WoW to −53,255, yet the options skew diverges by pricing aggressive downside tails. Intraday US Treasury 2s10s curve displays a bear steepener (+34.6bp) with the US 10Y yield holding near 4.996%, sustaining spot above the 155.00 handle. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; pronounced options put skew indicates structural downside hedging. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: BoJ leaves policy settings entirely unchanged with dovish guidance, prompting short covering toward the SMA20 at 157.14.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: CFTC COT data shows Leveraged Funds holding net long AUD positioning of +48,379 contracts, sitting at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.72. WoW net positioning contracted by −1,871 contracts as buying momentum stalled while spot dipped to 0.7129, below the SMA20 at 0.7172 but above the SMA50 at 0.7077. Options markets price elevated hedging demand, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 7.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.4%, generating a positive Volatility Risk Premium of +2.1%. The RBA holds a 4.35% policy rate against the Fed at 3.75% (+60bp carry advantage to AUD), but extended positioning in the upper historical decile leaves the currency vulnerable to liquidation. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; positioning exhaustion and high vol premium restrict upside follow-through. Catalyst: FOMC interest rate decision 16 Sep — hold widely expected. Risk: Leveraged funds resume net aggressive accumulation above +55k contracts.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Technical Compression + Policy Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1542, compressed directly against its 50-day SMA at 1.1537 and capped beneath its 20-day SMA at 1.1627 and 200-day SMA at 1.1636. Leveraged funds hold net short EUR exposure of −46,381 contracts, hovering at the 34th percentile of the 52-week range despite a WoW reduction of +6,403 contracts. Fed holds at 3.75%. Real policy rate differentials also favor the dollar at +1.35% versus the euro at +0.31%, maintaining structural headwinds against sustained euro appreciation. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry spreads favor downside expansion on a break of the 50-day moving average. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y release 16 Sep — forecast 2.8%. Risk: Spot closes decisively above the 1.1636 200-day SMA cluster.
